metadata.title: Global Contact Center Demand — Forecast Decision Intelligence Dashboard
metadata.executive_summary: Evaluation of ML models vs Manual forecasts for contact center volume.

sections.observation: Manual forecasts outperformed the aggregate ML system.
sections.conclusion: The current Manual forecast maintains statistical superiority.

sections.observation: Manual WAPE was 17.84%. ML WAPE was 21.11%. Manual outperformed ML in 79.8% of evaluated weeks.
sections.conclusion: Manual forecasts were more accurate than the aggregate ML system across 99 weeks, with high statistical confidence.
sections.decision_support: Persistently higher aggregate ML error was associated with more forecasting misses across the evaluation window. This should be considered when evaluating continued reliance on the current ML pipeline.
sections.recommendation: Retain the Manual Forecast as the primary production forecasting method.

sections.observation: V2_9_Prophet ranked first among 92 eligible models with a Composite Score of 75.32. V3_33_Prophet ranked second at 68.09.
sections.conclusion: V2_9_Prophet scored highest among 92 models, but its lead over the runner-up did not clear the policy's confidence threshold (p = 0.529839).
sections.decision_support: The non-significant margin (effect size 0.0087, below the 0.015 policy minimum) should be considered when evaluating whether a model change is operationally justified.
sections.recommendation: Recommendation omitted: confidence is Low. The composite ranking gap did not clear the Medium-confidence minimum required to justify a deployment recommendation.

sections.observation: Weekly actual volume had a coefficient of variation of 7.59% across 99 weeks, below the policy's 15% high-volatility trigger. 3 weeks were flagged as statistical anomalies (|z| > 2.5).
sections.conclusion: Demand volatility was mathematically stable across the evaluation window, validating the use of standard forecasting metrics.
sections.decision_support: The absence of extreme systemic volatility indicates the evaluation window represents a standard operating environment.
sections.recommendation: Proceed with standard model evaluation; volume variance is within acceptable bounds.

sections.observation: Mean weekly ML WAPE was 21.2% in normal weeks and 21.74% in anomaly weeks (n=3).
sections.conclusion: Forecast accuracy was not significantly degraded during anomalous demand periods.
sections.decision_support: The models demonstrated sufficient robustness against the limited volume anomalies observed in the evaluation window.
